arguments.message:
All support documentation has been reviewed. Three customer questions were identified:

1. Maya Reyes: Why is she being logged out of Cursor on other machines when signing in with Google SSO on a different device? (Urgent)
2. Daniel Park: Invoice PDF download button spins, never finishes.
3. Riya Sundaram: Is there a keyboard shortcut for inline edit? If not, feature request.

Drafting initial customer replies now based on KB articles. For ticket TCK-4827 (logout on device switch), there is no documented policy change about forced sign-out across devices—might be a bug. Will escalate if not fully resolved from docs. Let me know if you'd like deeper info or specific phrasing for any ticket.

arguments.subject: Re: why am I being logged out every time I switch machines? [TCK-4827]
arguments.body:
Hi Maya,

Thank you for reaching out and for being a Pro customer. I'm very sorry for the disruption to your workflow and the frustration this has caused.

There has not been a recent policy change regarding sign-in sessions across devices—signing in to Cursor with the same Google SSO account on multiple machines has always been supported, and you should NOT be getting logged out automatically on other devices just by switching machines.

What you're describing (silent logouts, agent threads disconnecting, sidebar disappearing) is not expected behavior and is not covered by any policy or planned update. Based on your report, this is likely a bug or a server-side session handling issue, possibly related to changes deployed in the last few days.

To investigate, here are a couple of quick clarifying questions:
1. Has anything about your Google account or security settings recently changed (e.g., password update, 2FA, security alert)?
2. Are you using private browsing/incognito modes, or any browser extensions that might clear cookies or interfere with session persistence?

In the meantime, I am escalating this ticket for urgent review by our support engineers, since it is impacting your work and may affect other users.

You can expect a follow-up from a human support engineer shortly. Thank you for your patience—please don't hesitate to add any new details or screenshots if the issue changes.

Best regards,
Lyra Support Bot
Cursor Support Team
